title: Indian opposition and citizens protest electoral roll revisions in Delhi
seoTitle: Delhi protest against voter list revisions

tea.why: Protesters are demonstrating against the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls and the alleged removal of millions of names.
tea.want: Demonstrators demand the restoration of old voter lists and the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.
tea.changed: Oct 31: Delhi Police stated that thousands of protesters were detained during demonstrations in the capital.

summary: Opposition parties, student groups, youth activists, and citizens have organised demonstrations across India, including in Delhi, over controversial voter list revisions. Organised by groups including the Cockroach Janta Party, student groups, and opposition leaders, the protesters condemn the removal of millions of names from electoral rolls through the Election Commission of India's Special Intensive Revision. Participants demand the resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the restoration of previous voter lists, alleging the process threatens voting rights and favors the ruling party. In response, the Election Commission stated that the exercise aims to improve voter list accuracy and allows wrongly removed voters to re-enroll, while ruling party officials rejected allegations of electoral bias. Demonstrators in Delhi faced a heavy police and border police presence, with thousands detained according to police statements.
demands: Resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar
Restoration of the old voter lists
An independent Election Commission to ensure free and fair elections
response: India's Election Commission stated the exercise aims to make voter lists more accurate and allows wrongly removed voters to re-enroll. The ruling Bharatiya Janata Party rejected allegations that the revision is intended to influence election results. According to Delhi Police, thousands were detained during protests in the capital.
